correctness.rationale: For any prime-power field, nonzero determinant-zero 2x2 matrices decompose uniquely into a projective column and row line, giving exactly one left/right generator pair. The determinant polar pairing is nondegenerate even in characteristic two and every generator plane is self-orthogonal. Direct finite-character orthogonality makes each plane-coset normal operator a q^2 Fourier multiplier on its own frequencies; summing weights proves all eigenvalues and multiplicities. Grid-support counting gives exact kernels and min-view uniqueness; comparing weighted grid sums proves every tightness case. The reconstruction constant factor is checked on the mean and nonzero cone separately. The standalone checker explicitly constructs incidence matrices and verifies entire integer normal spectra for q=2,3,4, including arbitrary irregular positive weights. Finite tests corroborate the algebraic proof, not the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The object is the natural affine maximal-null-plane tomography of functions on the split determinant quadratic space. All such measurements have intrinsic kernel on invertible frequencies, so the determinant-zero Fourier band is the maximal natural recoverable translation-invariant domain. The theorem classifies every weighted direction subset, gives an exact blind-spot dimension, proves the only two smallest injective designs, and classifies all tight designs. Unexpectedly, adding some opposite-ruling views worsens unweighted condition number from 1 to sqrt(2), while adding all restores tightness. These are structural and optimal acquisition facts rather than an arbitrary small table calculation; no broader signal recovery or arbitrary coset-erasure claim is asserted.
